paragraphs: I am a senior data engineer with nearly nine years of experience building production data pipelines, databases, and ML systems.

I have shipped a data-quality gate for a CLIA/CAP, HIPAA and SOC 2 regulated production platform serving external customers, a privacy-preserving ML service behind an encrypted REST API, and HPC pipelines processing terabyte-scale datasets. At SimTec I build data pipelines for industrial plant data from process historians and SCADA systems.
I focus on reproducibility, testing, monitoring, and data governance — the properties that separate prototypes from production systems.

projects.title: RAPID-CT: Brain Hemorrhage Detection
projects.description: Deep learning model that detects brain bleeds (intracranial hemorrhage) on CT scans. Served through a REST API that never sees patient identity, protected by split-key encryption.
projects.outcome: 98% accuracy against radiologist labels on 1,000+ CT scans; 60% less processing time per case.

case_study.problem: Detect intracranial hemorrhage on brain CT fast enough to support triage, without exposing patient identity.
case_study.architecture: CT images → de-identification → ResNet classifier → PII-blind REST API with two-key split encryption
case_study.results: 98% accuracy vs. radiologist labels; 60% faster per case

visuals.alt: Two copies of an axial brain CT scan side by side. Left: the scan, with bright blood in the ventricles and in the brain tissue beside them. Right: the same scan with a red-to-yellow heatmap over the blood and a dashed box labelled ICH.
visuals.caption: Axial brain CT with intracerebral and intraventricular hemorrhage (left) and the hemorrhage highlighted on the same slice (right).

projects.title: Regulated Sequencing Data-Quality Gate
projects.description: Automated quality gate for a clinical genomics platform: it checks every sequencing run and blocks poor-quality data before it reaches a clinical report. Runs in a regulated CLIA/CAP, HIPAA and SOC 2 environment.
projects.outcome: Processed 200–1,000 patient samples per week in production.

case_study.problem: Block low-quality sequencing runs before they reach clinical reporting.
case_study.architecture: DRAGEN output → Python/WDL QC metrics → pass/fail gates → platform workspace

nodes.label: Normalized model

nodes.label: Constraints
nodes.detail: Constraints protect integrity; indexes serve the queries.

nodes.label: SCD-2 history
nodes.detail: Temporal records keep every past version of a row.

nodes.label: Append-only ledger
nodes.detail: New rows are added; existing rows are never overwritten.

nodes.label: Deployed engines
nodes.detail: PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL/SQLite, MongoDB and time-series stores.

projects.description: Database schemas designed and deployed on five engines, from PostgreSQL and SQL Server to MongoDB and time-series stores. Built to keep full history: versioned records (SCD-2), append-only ledgers, strict constraints and indexes.
projects.outcome: Deployed for internal tools, reporting back-ends and research data platforms.

nodes.label: What it relies on

projects.description: Opening up neural networks to see how they reach a decision. For image classifiers: Grad-CAM and saliency maps. For transformers: logit lens, attention-head analysis, linear probes and activation patching.
projects.outcome: Used to confirm that medical-imaging models look at clinically relevant regions, and to study how language models represent and route information.

projects.title: Causal Gene Discovery Pipeline
projects.description: Pipeline that links mouse genetic association results (Diversity Outbred GWAS) with gene-expression data (bulk RNA-seq eQTL) to find the genes behind each signal. Checked with conditional analysis and bootstrapping; top candidates confirmed by qPCR.
projects.outcome: Found one new lncRNA and two protein-coding genes behind bone mineral density GWAS loci. Reviewer's Choice Abstract, ASHG 2025.

projects.title: Time Tracking Platform — Ledger Schema

nodes.label: Time entries
nodes.detail: Time entries are recorded with TIMESTAMPTZ throughout.

nodes.label: Append-only ledger
nodes.detail: Corrections supersede earlier entries; nothing is overwritten.

nodes.label: SCD-2 rates
nodes.detail: Billing rates are kept as temporal records.

nodes.label: No aggregates
nodes.detail: No aggregates are stored in the schema.

nodes.label: Metrics
nodes.detail: Estimation calibration, earned-value metrics and anomaly detection.

projects.description: Time-tracking application with estimate calibration, earned-value metrics and anomaly detection. Its 13-table PostgreSQL 16 schema keeps a full audit trail: time entries are an append-only ledger, billing rates are versioned (SCD-2), and no totals are stored.
projects.outcome: Eight behavioral invariants tested against a live PostgreSQL instance.

case_study.problem: Track time, rates and budgets with a correct audit history instead of mutable rows.
case_study.architecture: PostgreSQL 16: append-only time-entry ledger, SCD-2 rate records, no stored aggregates, TIMESTAMPTZ throughout
case_study.results: 8 behavioral invariants validated against live PostgreSQL
